item.title: Public Affairs & Policy Manager (Wales) - Not-For-Profit (Health Sector)
item.description: About the Role ‍ Ellwood Atfield is partnering with a leading not-for-profit organisation in the health sector to appoint a Public Affairs & Policy Manager. This is a key role leading policy and external affairs activity in Wales, with collaboration across UK-wide teams. ‍ The successful candidate will lead public affairs strategy, manage stakeholder relationships, and provide expert political and policy advice to senior leadership. You will oversee a small team and play an important role in shaping the organisation’s external engagement and policy positioning. ‍ This role offers the opportunity to influence health policy, build strong stakeholder relationships, and contribute to meaningful impact across the healthcare system. ‍ ‍ Key Responsibilities ‍ You will lead public affairs and policy activity in Wales, providing strategic insight and advice to internal and external stakeholders. You will build and maintain strong relationships with policymakers, government bodies, and partners across the health sector, ensuring the organisation is positioned as a credible and influential voice. ‍ You will provide high-quality political intelligence, policy analysis, briefings, and advice to senior leaders. The role will involve overseeing policy projects, consultations, stakeholder engagement, and external communications activity, while managing and supporting a small team to deliver high-quality work. Working closely with colleagues across the UK, you will contribute to a joined-up external affairs strategy and help ensure the organisation responds effectively to developments in the political and policy environment. ‍ ‍ About You ‍ We are looking for someone with a strong understanding of the Welsh political, public affairs, and health policy environment. You will have experience providing policy and strategic advice to senior stakeholders and be confident in building trusted relationships with senior external partners. ‍ You will bring excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce high-quality briefings and policy documents. You will have experience managing complex workstreams and delivering projects to a high standard, as well as the ability to lead or support a team. Welsh language skills are desirable but not essential. ‍ ‍ ‍ How to Apply ‍ To apply, please submit your CV via Ellwood Atfield. Suitable applicants will be invited to an initial briefing call with our team to discuss the role in more detail. ‍ Closing date: Monday 27 April 2026 Early applications are strongly encouraged , as shortlisting and interviews will take place on a rolling basis. ‍ ‍

item.title: Policy Adviser
item.description: ‍ The organisation ‍ Ellwood Atfield is proud to be partnering with the Confederation of Passenger Transport (CPT) in the search for a Policy Adviser. The CPT is a renowned membership body which exists to help the bus and coach industry to provide better journeys for all. We do this by representing around 800 members ensuring the issues that matter most to the industry are firmly on the political agenda, giving them practical advice and support, and bringing the industry together to build better solutions. Our dedicated teams in England, Scotland and Wales work closely with members at local and national levels to help them achieve the best possible operating environment. ‍ Our members include the largest multi-national transport operations along with small family run businesses. We also represent 150 suppliers who each provide dedicated products and services to the bus and coach industries. ‍ ‍ Working at CPT ‍ Our values matter to us. They help us achieve what our members have asked us to and deliver our very best both individually and as an organisation. We are: ‍ Ambitious to make things better for the passengers our industry serves Inclusive in seeking out different perspectives and; Always there when our members need us ‍ We ask every colleague to live to these values as part of their role and ask managers to enable their teams to do so. ‍ ‍ The opportunity ‍ This role comes at an exciting time to be working in the bus and coach sector. Our industry is essential to supporting economic growth, thriving communities and opportunities for all, and this is increasingly recognised among policy makers and opinion formers. ‍ CPT works closely with government at all levels to help the industry deliver to its full potential, and as a Policy Adviser you will build strong ties with the Department for Transport and other key stakeholders to develop and promote impactful policy initiatives which advance the priorities of CPT members and to ensure the sector’s interests are represented and reflected in government policy. ‍ ‍ Key responsibilities ‍ Develop policy papers and briefings, including collation of relevant third-party research, to influence national and regional decision makers and those that influence them. Engage with government departments to help deliver CPT’s policy goals, ensuring the organisation’s policy priorities are clearly understood by decision-makers and CPT is recognised as the lead expert organisation on bus and coach issues. Work with CPT members to seek views on policy and to gather evidence to support strategies and priorities, including collaborating with members’ in-house teams to make sure policy reflects the needs of the bus and coach industry. Develop authoritative and evidence-based submissions such as consultation responses and select committee submissions with member input and engagement. Provide policy support for CPT Regional Managers on key strategic policy issues to ensure CPT’S policy positions are understood at the local and regional level. Monitor, collect and utilise data relevant to the sector to: ensure CPT’s evidence base is up to date; inform CPT’s external communications activity; identify trends and emerging issues; develop dashboards and visualisations for colleagues and members; and support policy development and strategic decision-making. ‍ ‍ Person specification ‍ Excellent written communicator with strong attention to detail and experience writing reports, presentations and briefings. Ability to identify and communicate key challenges in a clear, informative, succinct yet impactful way. Skilled in using quantitative data to identify issues and trends, support a policy position, strengthen an evidence-base and tell a story. A self-starter with strong organisational skills with an ability to work to tight deadlines and work strategically. Experience in navigating public policy issues and problem solving either within government or as a key government stakeholder and influencer. Adept at maintaining relationships with multiple stakeholders with the ability to manage multiple viewpoints and to influence. Ability to think strategically and see the ‘bigger picture’. Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills. Experience of overseeing the delivery of research projects by contracted third parties. ‍ ‍ How to apply: ‍ To apply, please submit the form below and include a copy of your CV. Closing date: Friday 31st July 9:00am We will only be able to consider applications submitted via the online link attached and not sent via email. ‍ ‍ Ellwood Atfield is the leading headhunter for corporate affairs, communications, policy, and advocacy. item.title: Senior Communications and Engagement Manager
item.description: About the organisation: ‍ Ellwood Atfield is proud to be partnering with the Road Safety Trust, the UK's leading independent grant-giving charity dedicated to making roads and streets safer for everyone. ‍ Since 2014, the Road Safety Trust has invested more than £13 million in research, innovation and practical interventions that help reduce deaths and serious injuries on UK roads. As the organisation delivers its ambitious 2025–2028 strategy, communications and engagement have become central to achieving its mission of ensuring robust evidence influences policy, professional practice and decision-making across the road safety sector. ‍ Working for the Road Safety Trust means helping ensure that high-quality research translates into policies and practices that save lives. You will join a respected, ambitious organisation with a growing national profile and play a leading role in shaping how it communicates with government, practitioners, researchers, funders and the wider road safety community. ‍ ‍ The opportunity: ‍ The Senior Communications and Engagement Manager will be the operational lead for communications delivery and play a pivotal role in bringing the Communications and Engagement Strategy to life. Reporting to the Deputy CEO / Director of Communications and Engagement, you will translate strategic priorities into high-quality, well-planned communications that strengthen the Trust's influence and reputation. ‍ This is a varied and rewarding leadership role for someone who enjoys combining strategic thinking with hands-on delivery. You will oversee communications planning, media relations, digital channels, editorial standards, stakeholder engagement, events and knowledge-sharing activity, ensuring every piece of communication is evidence-led, accurate and impactful. ‍ ‍ Main responsibilities: ‍ Lead the delivery of the Trust's Communications and Engagement Strategy, ensuring communications align with organisational priorities and objectives. Drive media relations and high-quality content, translating complex research into engaging, evidence-led communications across multiple channels. Manage the Trust's digital and stakeholder communications, including the website, social media, newsletters and communications planning. Coordinate communications across colleagues, partners and suppliers, ensuring high-quality, timely delivery of campaigns, events and engagement activities. Measure communications impact and drive continuous improvement, using insight and performance data to enhance reach, influence and effectiveness. ‍ ‍ Key skills and experience required: ‍ Proven experience in senior communications, media relations and stakeholder engagement, ideally within a charity, public sector, research, policy or other evidence-led organisation. Exceptional writing and editorial skills, with the ability to translate complex research, policy and technical information into engaging communications for a range of audiences. Strong strategic planning and project management skills, with experience delivering integrated communications plans, managing multiple priorities and coordinating internal and external stakeholders. Experience managing media, digital and external communications, including websites, social media, newsletters, media enquiries and agency or supplier relationships. A self-starter with excellent judgement and relationship building skills, with the confidence to work with senior leaders, manage reputational issues and deliver high-quality communications in a collaborative environment. ‍ ‍ Benefit s: ‍ We are open to applications from candidates who wish to work full-time or 4-days/30-hours per week. 28 days annual leave entitlement plus bank holidays (Pro rata for part-time staff) 28 days full contractual sick pay and sickness income protection from the 15th week of illness. item.title: Policy Officer
item.description: ‍ The organisation: ‍ Ellwood Atfield is proud to be partnering with one of the UK’s largest trade associations within the manufacturing sector. The organisation exists to ensure the prosperity and competitiveness of the manufacturing sector; its members range from multi-national companies to SMEs and start-ups. The trade association prides itself on its ability to support these businesses, championing their interests whilst engaging with government, media and stakeholders at the UK and global level to influence policy decision making. ‍ ‍ The opportunity: ‍ This is an exciting opportunity for a recently graduated candidate with an interest in developing their policy career with a renowned trade association. As a Policy Officer, you will contribute to the development, analysis and delivery of a range of policy issues across the sector, including on areas such as skills and industry competitiveness. You will work alongside the Policy Manager and wider department to delivery across the organisation’s strategic policy priorities. ‍ Whilst developing strong working relationships with the organisation’s diverse members, you will contribute to the coordination of the policy team’s member committees to understand industry needs. As a Policy Officer, you will also conduct research and analysis to ensure policy recommendations are supported by solid evidence. You will play a key role in producing high-quality briefings, reports and consultation responses for both an internal and external audience. ‍ ‍ Key Responsibilities: ‍ To monitor, analyse, research and write regular briefings on relevant political and industry issues for members and across the organisation. To support the development policy positions, consultation responses and engagement materials in collaboration with members and other stakeholders. To communicate policy developments such as briefings and positions to both an internal and external audience. To support relevant committees on policy developments as required, including supporting the work and management of the Policy Co-ordination Committee. To support the delivery of the organisation’s National Apprenticeship Week event in parliament alongside the Policy Manager. Foster strong working relationships with members, policymakers and external stakeholders. Represent the trade association at relevant working group, stakeholder meetings and industry events. Coordinate and contribute to Committees, Working Groups and external working groups. Support and, where appropriate, lead engagement with government officials and partner organisations. Support the Policy Team’s planning and delivery of advocacy priorities, KPIs and political engagement. Collaborate effectively across departments to ensure alignment and impact of policy activity. ‍ ‍ Person Specification: ‍ Educated to degree level – ideally in Politics, Law, International Relations or a related subject. Strong written and verbal communication skills with excellent attention to detail and an ability to produce high-quality briefings and reports for a diverse audience. Ability to analyse complex political and regulatory information and translate into a clear policy narrative. Confident building relationships with senior stakeholders. Good working knowledge of UK Parliamentary and legislative processes. Strong organisational skills, able to manage priorities and deadlines. A proactive and self-motivated individual with an ability to work independently. ‍ ‍ How to apply: ‍ To apply, please submit the form below and include a copy of your CV. Closing date: Thursday 30th July 9:00am We will only be able to consider applications submitted via the online link attached and not sent via email. ‍ ‍

item.title: Head of Media
item.description: ‍ About The organisation: ‍ Ellwood Atfield is proud to partner with High Speed 2 (HS2 Ltd), the organisation delivering Britain’s new high-speed railway between London and the Midlands, one of the UK’s largest infrastructure programmes. As well as improving rail capacity, HS2 will shorten journey times between a number of Britain’s major population centres, boost the economy and create thousands of jobs. ‍ HS2 Ltd is making good progress in resetting the programme, with a renewed focus on delivery discipline, cost control and ensuring every pound spent delivers value for the taxpayer. As this essential part of the national rail network takes shape, communicating that story, honestly and confidently, to the public, media, Parliament and Government, has never mattered more. ‍ The opportunity: ‍ HS2 Ltd is seeking a Head of Media to provide strategic leadership across its Media Relations and Digital Media and Content teams, ensuring delivery of the External Affairs Directorate’s (EAD) communications and engagement plan. The role supports the business in achieving its goals in a highly regulated and highly scrutinised environment, through effective engagement with external media and HS2’s own digital channels. ‍ Reporting to the External Affairs Director and sitting on the EAD Leadership Team, the Head of Media will lead a team of 11 which is split across media, digital media and content, and will provide guidance and direction to the EAD Director, CEO, HS2 Executive Committee, Chair and Senior Leadership Team on media relations and digital media activity. ‍ This is a rare opportunity for an experienced media leader to shape how one of the UK’s most nationally significant infrastructure programmes is understood, at a pivotal moment in its delivery. ‍ ‍ Main responsibilities: ‍ Develop and lead the media relations and digital media function for HS2, ensuring full alignment with the wider communications and engagement programme.
